abstract: Seed germination is a critical step of plant development that is highly sensitive to water availability. During this delicate transition, water stress responses are tightly regulated by multilevel molecular networks that integrate environmental cues into developmental adaptations. Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) play a positive signaling role in seed germination, yet their influence on germination under water stress remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the involvement of ROS in Arabidopsis thaliana seed germination upon reproducibly reducing water potential using polyethylene glycol (PEG). The data show that delayed germination under water stress is not simply a consequence of reduced water uptake. Instead, water stress triggers coordinated reprogramming events characterized by altered H2O2 homeostasis, particularly in peroxisomes, which functionally mediates a rebalancing of ABA and GA metabolism toward developmental slowdown. A weighted gene co-expression network analysis of water-stress transcriptomic dynamics identified a gene hub associated with H2O2 production during germination, shedding light on multiple oxygen- and redox-related processes that are strongly linked to transcriptional and translational attenuation. Collectively, this study unveils a role for regulating peroxisomal H2O2 homeostasis in Arabidopsis seed water stress responses, offering new perspectives for improving crop resilience to environmental constraints.
